text: Every enterprise design eventually needs a path back to on-premises — a data center, a branch office, another cloud. This lesson covers the two mechanisms for that: a dedicated private circuit, ExpressRoute or Direct Connect, and a site-to-site VPN tunnel, and how to actually decide between them for a given workload.

These aren't just an expensive version and a cheap version of the same link. A dedicated circuit never touches the public internet — it runs over private infrastructure through a connectivity provider. A VPN tunnel rides over the public internet with IPsec encrypting everything inside it. They differ in failure characteristics, SLA, and lead time to stand up, and a real decision weighs all three.

ExpressRoute connects on-premises to Azure through a peering location, where a connectivity provider establishes a circuit. Private peering reaches Azure VNets; Microsoft peering reaches public services like Azure Storage without a public IP route. The bandwidth, SKU tier, and peering location are a conversation with the provider first — physical circuit provisioning is the slow part, weeks to months, not minutes.

AWS Direct Connect is the same idea on AWS's terms. A private virtual interface, a VIF, reaches a VPC through a virtual private gateway or Direct Connect Gateway; a public VIF reaches AWS services like S3 without touching the internet. Direct Connect Gateway matters once there's more than one VPC or region — it lets one physical connection serve many attachments instead of needing a separate connection per VPC.

Site-to-site VPN trades the dedicated circuit's throughput ceiling for speed and cost: both clouds support it natively, and it's typically live in hours once the on-premises firewall supports IPsec, versus the weeks a dedicated circuit takes. High, sustained, predictable throughput justifies a dedicated circuit; a branch office or a site that just needs connectivity fast is usually VPN.

For production traffic that can't tolerate an outage, enterprise designs typically use both — VPN configured as automatic failover for the dedicated circuit, because a dedicated circuit isn't immune to being cut either. Real resilience comes from two independent paths. Next lesson turns to DNS across multiple accounts and VNets.
